counterfactual_missing_items: insufficient information on the patient's family history
decisive_items: a destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus, forming a large soft-tissue mass
response.rationale: R5 is the champion because it has more raw support spans that match the vignette, including the destructive lesion and rapid enlargement of the mass. R3 is the runner-up because it also has some matching raw support spans, but fewer than R5. The decisive items are the destructive lesion, heterogeneous enhancement, and rapid enlargement, which are more consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma than Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.why: Orbital cellulitis is unlikely due to the lack of response to antibiotic treatment and the presence of a destructive lesion on imaging.
Ewing sarcoma is a possible diagnosis, but it has fewer matching raw support spans than R5 and R3.
